blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Conflict at work is unavoidable. What changes everything is how we handle it. A small issue that is ignored can turn into a toxic relationship, while a difficult conversation that happens early and honestly can rebuild trust in thirty minutes.

A professional approach starts with preparation. What is the real issue? What is my goal? What facts can I share? What do I need to listen to? The meeting itself should be private, calm and respectful — never in front of others.

Language makes a huge difference. Instead of "You always interrupt me", say "I would like to talk about what happened in yesterday's meeting." Softer language is not weaker — it is what allows the other person to stay open instead of defensive.

items.q: According to the text, what makes the real difference with workplace conflict?
items.why: "What changes everything is how we handle it." — o conflito em si é inevitável.

items.q: What does the text say a professional approach starts with?
items.why: "A professional approach starts with preparation."

items.q: Where should the difficult conversation take place?
items.why: "The meeting itself should be private, calm and respectful — never in front of others."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Using gentle language shows you are weak.
Softer language keeps the other person open.
Ignoring a small issue can make it worse.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz claramente que "softer language is not weaker".

items.q: The contrast between "You always interrupt me" and "I would like to talk about…" suggests that…
options: meetings are better than one-to-one talks
facts do not matter in a difficult conversation
how you phrase an issue affects whether the other person defends themselves
you should avoid mentioning problems at all
items.why: Inferência: o exemplo mostra que a formulação diplomática evita a reação defensiva.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James preparando uma mediação entre dois gestores seniores. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let me write down how I want to open this. Two of the best managers we have, and they haven't spoken properly in weeks. If I get the first two minutes wrong, one of them shuts down and the other gets defensive — so the wording really matters.

I won't start with the problem. I'll start with the shared goal. Something like: "Thank you both for making the time. I know this hasn't been easy. Before we get into what happened, could we agree that we all want the project to succeed?" That gives us common ground before we touch anything difficult.

Then I'll keep the language neutral. Not "you did this", not "you were wrong" — just "I'd like to understand how each of you saw the meeting." And I'll listen far more than I talk. De-escalation starts with listening, not with me explaining who is right.

My real goal isn't to decide a winner. It's to get them back to working together. If we can rebuild a little trust today, the rest will follow.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does James think the first two minutes matter so much?
options: Because he wants to record the meeting
Because the managers have little time
Because the wrong wording could make one shut down and the other defensive
Because he has to leave early
items.why: "If I get the first two minutes wrong, one of them shuts down and the other gets defensive."

items.q: How does James plan to open the conversation?
options: By listing the facts of the dispute
By stating who is at fault
By asking each manager to apologise
items.why: "I won't start with the problem. I'll start with the shared goal."

items.q: According to James, de-escalation starts with…
items.why: "De-escalation starts with listening, not with me explaining who is right."

items.q: Why does James avoid phrases like "you did this" or "you were wrong"?
options: Because neutral language keeps the managers from getting defensive
Because he isn't sure of the facts
Because he is not allowed to blame anyone
Because he wants the meeting to be shorter
items.why: Inferência: ele escolhe linguagem neutra para manter os dois abertos, não na defensiva.

items.q: What does James see as the real success of the mediation?
options: Getting the two managers working together again
Producing a written record of the dispute
items.why: "My real goal isn't to decide a winner. It's to get them back to working together."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "HR asked James to run a mediation between the two teams." A mediation is…
options: a process where a neutral person helps resolve a dispute
items.why: Mediation = mediação: um terceiro neutro ajuda as partes a chegar a um acordo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "If we don't fix this now, it will ___ to the director's office."
items.why: To escalate = escalar: o problema sobe para um nível mais alto.

items.q: "She filed a formal grievance with HR." A grievance is…
items.why: Grievance = queixa formal registrada, normalmente com o RH.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Once both sides calmed down, they finally found some ___ to build on."
items.why: Common ground = ponto em comum, base compartilhada para avançar.

items.q: "His tone was defensive from the start." Defensive here means…
options: quick to protect himself and resist criticism
items.why: Defensive = defensivo: reage protegendo-se, em vez de ouvir.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas difíceis. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's try to de-escalate this before it gets worse." To de-escalate means to…
options: reduce the tension in a situation
items.why: De-escalate = desescalar, baixar a tensão.

items.q: "I don't want to fall out with a colleague over this." To fall out with someone means to…
options: have an argument and stop being friendly
items.why: Fall out with = brigar/romper relações com alguém.

items.q: "Can we talk it through before the meeting?" To talk something through means to…
options: decide it without the other person
discuss it fully to reach understanding
items.why: Talk something through = conversar a fundo até se entender.

items.q: "After a difficult year, they slowly began to rebuild trust." To rebuild trust means to…
items.why: Rebuild trust = reconstruir a confiança que havia se perdido.

items.q: "Please don't bring up old issues in this meeting." To bring something up means to…
options: raise or mention it in conversation
items.why: Bring up = trazer à tona, mencionar um assunto.
